text:
liz (cs): Heads-up — Nimbus (acct:nimbus-prod) opened a high-priority ticket: after yesterday's canary (v2.3.1 -> model svc), they see invoice numbers dropped from 80% of responses + intermittent 502/503s. Customer is very upset. Escalating for immediate triage.

ops-bot: deploy canary v2.3.1 started at 2026-02-11T03:12:07Z on cluster eu-west-1-gpu-pool. Canary traffic 5%. Rollout stage: canary->monitoring.

vikram (infra): Thanks. Can someone paste the customer's repro and request-ids? Need to see gateway/infra traces. Priority: capture headers `x-request-id`, `x-server-latency-ms`.

lia (support): Repro steps from customer (copied):
1) POST /v1/generate with model `redwood-v2-large`
2) prompt: `Summarize invoice #<ID> and list line items` (they're seeing "Invoice for" but missing the id)
3) example curl:```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-large","input":"Summarize invoice #INV-12345 and list line items"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | jq '.'
```
Customer included request-ids: `req-72f4c6`, `req-72f4d1`, logs show responses with body missing `INV-12345` and with HTTP 502 at times. They said latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.2s for those calls.

autoticket-bot: created INC-2026-0192 for Nimbus escalation, severity: high, assignees: eng-runtime.

sara (engineer): Quick notes from runtime side: recent change in tokenization + prompt-truncation heuristics landed in canary. Hypothesis: KV-cache eviction thresholds + new batching optimization sometimes drop early tokens (invoice IDs) when prompts contain `#` or `INV-` patterns in long histories. Also seeing a rare NGINX upstream 502 when a backend worker OOMs under a particular batch size.

vikram (infra): OOM traces: attaching snippet (from infra logs) —
```
[2026-02-11T03:14:05Z] worker-7 PID 2381 OOM kill: killed process 2386 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:12G anon-rss:9.7G
Backtrace: schedule, oom_reaper
Headers: x-request-id=req-72f4d1 x-server-latency-ms=1234
```

mike (billing): Customer noticed duplicate token billing spikes for the same timeframe. Looks like their client retried on 502s causing double counting. We should offer a credit while we investigate. If it's a platform retry bug we'll refund.

neal (pm): Customer impact looks like: missing invoice IDs (major correctness), increased latency, and billing surprise. Need comms template, mitigation steps, and ETA to rollback or hotfix.

sara (engineer): Immediate mitigations I recommend (order matters):
- 1) Pin Nimbus to previous model variant: `x-model-variant: redwood-v2-legacy` via API header or set account override in console. That avoids the new tokenization path.
- 2) For platform reliability: temporarily reduce canary batch-size to 1 for eu-west GPU pool and increase memory guardrails. I can push a config at infra level now.
- 3) Prompt-side mitigation for customers: add a sentinel token before invoice IDs, e.g. prepend `---START-ID---INV-12345` or wrap ID in backticks to force it into preserved tokens.

lia (support): Draft customer message for approval: "We're sorry — after a recent internal rollout some responses omitted invoice IDs and you may have seen timeouts. We've pinned your account to the prior model variant and provisioned a fallback; we will issue credits for duplicate tokens and follow up by EOD with a permanent fix. To help repro, could you paste any `x-request-id` values?" :thumbsup:

vikram (infra): Pushing immediate infra config: canary batch-size -> 1 on eu-west-1 at 03:18Z. Watching memory.

ops-bot: config change applied: eu-west-1 canary.batch_size=1 by vikram at 2026-02-11T03:18:42Z.

sara (engineer): I deployed a hotfix branch that restores previous truncation behavior and disables the new tokenization shortcut for canary traffic. Patch rolled to canary at 03:20:50Z. Initial checks against provided repro: invoice IDs preserved in 9/10 tests, latency back to ~140ms.

lia (support): Updated Nimbus: "We've pinned your traffic away from the canary and applied a temporary fix. Please verify on your side and share any failing `x-request-id`s. We will apply a credit for duplicate requests while we review logs. Apologies for the disruption."

mike (billing): I'll prepare a provisional credit equal to the usage spike and hold final settlement pending root-cause.

neal (pm): Good. Ask eng to run a targeted regression test suite across tokens with `#` and `INV-` patterns and produce a before/after diff. Also let's schedule an all-hands postmortem if this hits more customers.

sara (engineer): Will run AB sweep and post results in eng-runtime channel. Early summary: hotfix reduced missing-ID rate from ~22% -> ~1.5% on canary sample. Will follow up with detailed logs.

liz (cs): Customer replied: confirmed IDs back in results for our sample, appreciate the quick action. They've accepted provisional credit. Closing loop here and will update Nimbus once we validate full roll-forward. Thanks team. :heart:

ops-bot: ticket INC-2026-0192 status changed to investigating -> mitigated by vikram,sara at 2026-02-11T03:28:58Z.
